pros: Formula language works across tables and inside plain text
Buttons and automations run actions without an external tool
Packs pull live data from Slack, Jira, Gmail and Salesforce
Per Doc Maker pricing keeps editors and viewers free
cons: Large docs with many rows become slow to load
No company wide page tree; permissions are set per doc
Steep learning curve for anyone building beyond simple tables
verdict_line: Pick Coda if you need a document that computes, tracks and triggers actions like a small app rather than a page of text.

pros: Notes are plain Markdown files stored on your own device
Core app is free, including for commercial use
Backlinks, graph view and daily notes reward long term use
Thousands of community plugins add databases, Kanban and AI
Fully offline with instant search across large vaults
cons: No real-time collaboration, comments or shared permissions
Comfortable setup depends on volunteer maintained plugins
No built in AI; plugins need your own API key
No web version; the app must be installed
verdict_line: Pick Obsidian if you want a personal knowledge base in Markdown files you own, with no vendor lock in and no subscription required.

pros: Any line in a doc becomes a task with two way links
Fifteen plus task views including Gantt, workload and table
Automation builder handles status, field and date triggers
Dashboards report on structured task data out of the box
Brain answers questions across tasks, docs and connected apps
cons: Doc editor is weaker than dedicated writing tools
Dense interface with many settings to configure
AI is an add on charged above the seat price
Large workspaces can load slowly at times
verdict_line: Pick ClickUp if you want tasks, docs, chat and dashboards in one workspace and project management matters more than writing polish.

pros: Deep Jira links between requirements, issues and release notes
Space and page level permissions with audit logs
Data Center edition can run on your own infrastructure
Marketplace with thousands of add on apps
Rovo AI searches across Confluence, Jira and connected tools
cons: Editor is slower and more rigid than modern rivals
Databases feature lags Notion and Coda tables
Every reader needs a paid seat as headcount grows
Search ranks stale pages highly without active curation
verdict_line: Pick Confluence if your company already runs on Jira and needs a governed wiki with granular permissions and a self hosted option.

pros: Document verification with expiry keeps content trustworthy
Knowledge panel lists stale, unverified and duplicate pages
Ask answers questions with citations, including from Slack
Clean minimal editor without database distractions
cons: No permanent free plan, only a trial
No relational databases, automations or project views
Limited integrations beyond Slack and embeds
No self hosted option for regulated environments
verdict_line: Pick Slite if you want a pure knowledge base that nudges owners to keep pages verified and current instead of an all in one workspace.

pros: Native Mac, iPad and iPhone apps with reliable offline editing
Documents look polished with page styles and typography built in
Shared links render as clean, password protectable mini sites
Clean Markdown, PDF and Word export makes leaving easy
cons: No relations, rollups or formulas in Collections
Team collaboration and permissions trail Notion and Confluence
Few integrations and no automation builder
Free plan block limits push regular users to pay
verdict_line: Pick Craft if you want the best looking, fastest offline document editor on Apple devices and do not need databases.
